payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the image been transformed from the source into a convincingly pencil-drawn rendering across the scene?
node.criteria: Pass only if pencil-like strokes, outlines, and drawn shading consistently replace the source's photographic texture across the scene, so the image reads as a pencil drawing. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that transformation, or if the treatment is only partial or weak—for example, desaturation or grain with substantial photographic or filtered appearance remaining. Unknown only if the source/edit evidence is insufficient to judge the transformation.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images for fulfillment of the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Assess the rendering of the scene as a whole; monochrome or grain alone is not sufficient evidence of complete fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is substantially desaturated and has a grainy, softened appearance, but the objects retain photographic shading and texture. Pencil-like strokes and drawn outlines do not consistently replace the photographic rendering across the scene.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s evidence identifies a real but incomplete edit: the image is desaturated and grainy, while much of its shading and texture remains photographic. The binary pass/fail criterion collapses that partial progress into “fail,” which conflicts with the rubric’s distinction between no progress and incomplete fulfillment. Make the decision explicitly distinguish no visible requested transformation, partial transformation, and convincing scene-wide pencil rendering; treat monochrome or grain alone as insufficient for completion, but count them alongside any actual drawing-like changes when judging progress. Keep “unknown” for insufficient visual evidence, not for a weak edit. The trace is valid and queried with no transport or dependency failure, so this is a criterion/label-mapping issue, not missing evidence. Do not infer atomic ground truth from the aggregate reference label; use the visible source/edit comparison and rubric to calibrate the node’s outcome."}
